Clickacode widget operations

Tables

The (+) menu

  • Add a column
    Type a $-expression for a new column, with autocomplete.
  • Show / hide fields
    Tick fields on and off; Show all, Hide all.

A column's ▾ menu

  • Search a column
    A search in the column's scope, with its operator and and / or composition.
  • Tally
    Tick values to keep or exclude them; sort and narrow the tally.
  • Sort
    Asc / Desc rewrites the line in place; the insert rows write a sorted copy.
  • Group By
  • Change Type
    Read the column as int / float / str / bool, in place or as a new column.
  • Subcolumns
    Spread a column of records across several sub-columns.
  • Expand list items into rows / collapse them back
    A column of lists becomes one row per element.
  • Compute
    Sum, min, max, mean, median, percentiles, counts, histogram and the rest, kept under the column.
  • A custom aggregation
    Type any expression over the column.
  • Per-group answers
    On a splatted column, one answer per group becomes a column.
  • Unique / Tally
    Write set($) or Counter($) as a line.
  • Insert Left / Insert Right
  • Remove

A row's ▾ menu

  • Extract Item
    Take one row out as a line of its own.
  • Delete, Pop, Extract Cells, Use as Headers
    The rest of the row menu, and the same for the last row.

The search box and action bar

  • Search
    A predicate with $, $i, $$ and $$$; the Filter line is written as you type.
  • First match only
  • Filter
  • Count
  • Delete All
    The list without the matched rows.
  • Find Indices
    The positions of the matched rows.
  • Extract
    The columns on show, as a list.
  • Join
    The cells joined with a separator.
  • Any / All / If any / If all
  • Loop
    A for loop over the matched rows, with or without the index.
  • Pick
    Click cells to assemble an expression over a matched row.

Headers and cells

  • Edit a column expression
    Double-click a header to rewrite it.
  • Reorder columns by dragging
  • Resize a column
  • Load more rows
    Paging past 50 rows.
  • Drag out
    Drag a cell, a row, a column header, an aggregation or a tally row into the code.

Strings

The string itself

  • Literal drag
    Drag across the top half of characters to match them literally.
  • Fuzzy drag
    Drag across the bottom half to match a character class.
  • Index drag
    Drag with the index tool to make a slice.
  • Chain segments
    Start a new drag at the end of a selection.
  • Resize a segment
    Drag its handles.
  • Segment menu
    Change a segment's repetition (1, ?, *, +, exact, range) or character class; split or delete it.
  • Pick
    Click chips of the first match (start, end, prefix, groups, suffix) to build an expression.
  • Drag out
    Drag a match or a chip into the code.

The search box

  • Type a search
    A regex, a substring, a slice or an expression; the Substrs line is written as you type.
  • First match / Match case / Capture groups
  • Replace
    Open the replace box and write re.sub.
  • Map
    The replace box as a mapping over the matches.

The action bar

  • Match Objects / Substrs / Indexes
    The matches as objects, strings or index pairs.
  • Count
  • Split
  • Delete
  • Filter
    Keep the elements of a list of strings that match.
  • Any / All / If any / If all
  • Loop
    Loop over the matches.
  • Fetch URL / Read Filepath
    Read a string that names a place, as text, JSON, CSV or Excel.

Objects and tuples

  • Add a field
    Type an accessor, with autocomplete over the object's attributes.
  • Edit / remove / reorder fields
  • Drag out
    Drag a field into the code; drag a tuple element or the whole tuple.
  • Nested visualizers
    A string in a table cell, a table in a tuple: the child works as it would alone and the code it writes reads through the parent.

The editor

  • The linked line
    A generated line keeps rewriting as the gesture continues; the chain icon unlinks and relinks.
  • The #%click comment
    A line's saved columns or fields, folded to a chip.
  • Focus
    Widgets away from the cursor draw small; a click pins one.
  • Loops
    The slider picks which iteration a widget inside a loop shows; pin an iteration.
  • Drop a URL, a browser tab or a file into the code
    Writes the line that reads it.
  • The console
    stdin and stdout for the program.
  • Live-only mode
    Visualizers without any affordance that writes code.
  • Errors
    An uncaught exception drawn at the line that raised it.
  • NumPy and pandas
    Read-only summaries.
